title: used to — Past Habits and States
grammarTitle: used to — Past Habits and States
grammarNote:
"Used to + infinitive" — говорим о том, что происходило РЕГУЛЯРНО в прошлом, но БОЛЬШЕ НЕ ПРОИСХОДИТ.

① Прошлые привычки (больше не актуальны):
   "I used to walk to school." (Сейчас езжу на автобусе.)
   "She used to play piano every evening." (Сейчас перестала.)

② Прошлые состояния (изменились):
   "He used to be very shy." (Сейчас уверенный.)
   "There used to be a cinema here." (Сейчас нет.)

Образование:
✅ Утверждение: Subject + USED TO + base verb
"I used to smoke." · "She used to live here."

✅ Отрицание: Subject + DIDN'T USE TO + base verb (без d!)
"I didn't use to like vegetables." · "He didn't use to exercise."

✅ Вопрос: DID + Subject + USE TO + base verb?
"Did you use to live here?" · "Did she use to study music?"

⚠️ Не путай: "used to DO" ≠ "be used to DOING"
"I used to swim." = раньше плавал (больше нет)
"I am used to swimming." = привык плавать (сейчас привычно)

rows.example: We used to walk to school every day. (now we take a bus)

rows.form: Past state (situation that no longer exists)
rows.example: She used to be shy. (now she is confident)

rows.form: Past possession (you no longer have it)
rows.example: They used to have a big garden. (they moved to a flat)

rows.form: Past belief (you no longer believe this)
rows.example: I used to think Nauryz was boring. (now I love it)
She used to dislike cooking — now she loves it.

rows.form: Can be replaced with "would" for habits (NOT states)
rows.example: We used to sing / We would sing (but NOT: I used to be tall → ✗ I would be tall)

rows.form: Rule: did not use to + BASE form
rows.example: She didn't use to celebrate Nauryz. ✓ / She didn't used to celebrate. ✗

rows.form: Meaning: something was NOT a past habit
rows.example: My family didn't use to have a yurt. (they never had one)
She never used to cook. ✓ (informal but acceptable)
He used not to attend celebrations. (formal British English)

rows.form: Contrast: didn't use to vs Past Simple negative
rows.example: She didn't use to eat meat (habit). / She didn't eat meat yesterday (single event).
She usedn't to... ✗ (not used in modern English)

grammarExtra.title: Question: "Did you use to?" (NOT "Did you used to?")

rows.form: Rule: Did + subject + use to + BASE form?
rows.example: Did you use to play traditional games? ✓
Did you used to play? ✗ → Did you use to play? ✓
What did you use to do at Nauryz? Where did they use to live?
Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
Used you to celebrate Nauryz? (very formal, old-fashioned)

rows.form: Checking meaning: "Did you use to...?" confirms a past habit
rows.example: Did she use to be a teacher? — Yes, she did. Now she's retired.

grammarExtra.title: used to vs Past Simple — Key Difference

rows.form: "used to" = repeated past habit or long state
rows.example: He used to smoke for 10 years. (habit over time)
He smoked a cigarette at the party. (one time)
She used to be nervous about English. (she isn't now)

rows.form: Past Simple has no implication about now
rows.example: She was nervous at the exam. (no info about now)
when I was young / as a child / in those days / back then
yesterday / last year / in 1969 / three years ago

grammarTip:
Главная ловушка — в вопросах и отрицаниях "use to" (без d!):

❌ "Did you USED TO live here?" → ✅ "Did you USE TO live here?"
❌ "I didn't USED TO like it." → ✅ "I didn't USE TO like it."

В утверждении: ✅ "I USED TO swim every day."
В отрицании: ✅ "I didn't USE TO swim."
В вопросе: ✅ "Did you USE TO swim?"

exercises.text: My grandmother ___ make Nauryz kozhe in an outdoor cauldron.
My family ___ have a yurt — we always set up tables outside.
___ you ___ play traditional games at Nauryz as a child?
exercises.hint: Question: Did + subject + "use to" (not "used to") + base form.

exercises.instruction: Choose the sentence that uses "used to" correctly.
opts: She used to went to school by bus.
She used to go to school by bus.
She used to going to school by bus.
She use to go to school by bus.
exercises.correct: She used to go to school by bus.
exercises.hint: "Used to" is always followed by BASE form (infinitive).

opts: He was shy in the past but is not now
He will be shy in the future
exercises.correct: He was shy in the past but is not now
exercises.hint: "Used to" always implies the situation is different now.

exercises.instruction: Complete with "used to" or "didn't use to".
exercises.text: Kamila ___ love dancing as a child, but now it's her passion.
exercises.hint: Negative of 'used to': didn't use to (no 'd' on 'use').

exercises.instruction: Which sentence is about a past state (not a habit)?
exercises.text: Choose the "used to" sentence describing a STATE.
opts: She used to cook every morning.
He used to run to school.
exercises.hint: A STATE = a condition/situation (be, have, know, believe) — not an action verb.

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct time expression with "used to".
exercises.text: She ___ play in the yard ___ she was a child.
exercises.hint: "When I was young/a child" is a typical time expression with "used to".

exercises.text: "___ she use to celebrate Nauryz with her whole family?"
exercises.hint: Question with "used to": Did + subject + use to (BASE)?

exercises.text: Amir ___ live in Uralsk — he is from Aktobe.
exercises.hint: Negative 'used to' for a past state that wasn't true.

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form of "used to".
exercises.text: In those days, people ___ travel by horse — there were no cars.
exercises.hint: Affirmative "used to" for a past habit that no longer exists.

exercises.text: "Did you use to sing at Nauryz celebrations?" — "___, I did. We always sang traditional songs."
exercises.hint: Short answer to "Did you use to...?" is "Yes, I did." / "No, I didn't."

questions.text: My family ___ celebrate Nauryz with a big yurt.
questions.hint: Affirmative: subject + used to + BASE form.

questions.text: She ___ cook traditional food — she preferred modern restaurants.
___ your family ___ have big Nauryz celebrations when you were young?
questions.hint: Question form: Did + subject + use to + base form.

questions.text: "They used to be very poor" describes:
opts: A past state that is no longer true
questions.correct: A past state that is no longer true
questions.hint: "used to be" = a state in the past that has changed.

questions.text: "Did she used to sing?" is correct.
questions.hint: In questions: "Did she use to sing?" — no "d" on "use" because "did" carries past meaning.

questions.text: Which sentence describes a HABIT (not a state)?
opts: He used to know the answer.
They used to visit their grandmother every Sunday.
We used to have a dog.
questions.correct: They used to visit their grandmother every Sunday.
questions.hint: A habit = a repeated action. "Visit every Sunday" is a regular repeated action.

questions.text: "used to" is used for a ___ past habit or state.
questions.hint: "used to" refers to something that happened repeatedly or was true for a long period.

questions.text: He ___ smoke, but he stopped ten years ago.
questions.hint: Positive "used to" for a past habit that has stopped.

questions.text: Which time expression is typical with "used to"?
questions.hint: "When I was young/a child/in those days" are typical with "used to".

questions.text: She ___ study very hard — now she is more relaxed.
questions.hint: Positive "used to" + BASE form for a past habit.

questions.text: "would" can replace "used to" for past STATES as well as habits.
questions.hint: "would" can only replace "used to" for HABITS, not states. Not: "I would be shy" ✗

questions.text: What does "She used to be a teacher" tell us about now?
opts: She is no longer a teacher
questions.correct: She is no longer a teacher
questions.hint: "Used to" always implies the situation has changed — she is NOT a teacher now.
Negative: didn't use to + BASE form.
"used to" is always followed by BASE form (infinitive without "to").

questions.text: "I used to think English was difficult" means:
opts: I still think English is difficult
I no longer think English is difficult
I will always think English is difficult
English was difficult for one day
questions.correct: I no longer think English is difficult
questions.hint: "used to think" = past belief that has changed.

opts: Did you used to play kokpar?
Did you use to play kokpar?
Were you used to play kokpar?
Do you used to play kokpar?
questions.correct: Did you use to play kokpar?
questions.hint: Question: Did + subject + use to (not "used to") + BASE form?
